claims.text: Hadrian's Library is a monumental ruin on the north side of the Acropolis, commissioned by the Roman Emperor Hadrian in 132 AD.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The building followed a Roman forum architectural style, featuring an inner courtyard surrounded by columns with a decorative oblong pool in the middle.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The library itself was located on the eastern side, containing special cupboards and shelves that held ancient rolls of papyrus 'books'.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The interior would have been stunning, as the ceilings were originally made of gilded wood and the walls were covered in marble and vibrant paintings.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The complex was seriously damaged by the Herulian invasion in the year 267 and its ruins were eventually incorporated into the Roman city walls.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During Byzantine times, the site was repurposed and three different churches were built here, including a 12th-century cathedral known as Megali Panagia.
claims.subject: self
